# POST /api/v1/orgs/{org}/rename

Rename an organization

**Module:** [routers](../modules/routers.md) · **Auth:** bearer (reqToken + reqOrgOwnership) · **ID:** `ep-032`

## Request

| Param | Location | Type | Required |
|-------|----------|------|----------|
| org | path | string | True |

**Request Body** (`application/json`) — `RenameOrgOption`

| Field | Type | Required | Validation |
|-------|------|----------|------------|
| `new_name` | string | True | Required |

## Response

**204** — empty

- **403** — Not org owner or site admin
- **422** — Name already exists, reserved, or contains invalid chars/pattern

## Workflow

| Step | Module | Component | Type | Details |
|------|--------|-----------|------|---------|
| 1 | [routers](../modules/routers.md) | orgAssignment(true) + reqToken + reqOrgOwnership | utility | Resolves org; Validates token; Checks org ownership or site admin |
| 2 | [modules](../modules/modules.md) | bind(api.RenameOrgOption{}) | utility | Parses JSON body; Validates Required field |
| 3 | [routers](../modules/routers.md) | org.Rename | controller | Calls user_service.RenameUser with org user and new name |
| 4 | [services](../modules/services.md) | user_service.RenameUser | service | Validates username usability; If only capitalization change: updates name col + repo owner names; Otherwise: starts transaction, checks existence, updates repo owner names, creates user redirect, updates agit refs, updates container names, updates user name/lower_name cols, renames filesystem directory, commits transaction |

## Business Rules

| Rule | Category | Condition |
|------|----------|-----------|
| Organization username must be usable (not reserved, valid chars, valid pattern) | validation | user_model.IsUsableUsername(org.Name) returns error |
| Organization username must not already exist as any user type | validation | user_model.IsUserExist(ctx, 0, org.Name) returns true |
| reqOrgOwnership requires user to be org owner or site admin | authorization | !ctx.IsUserSiteAdmin() && !IsOrganizationOwner(ctx, orgID, ctx.Doer.ID) |
| Rename with only capitalization change skips transaction and redirect creation | business_logic | strings.EqualFold(newUserName, u.Name) |

## Error Handling

| Trigger | Status | Response | Retryable |
|---------|--------|----------|-----------|
| New name already taken | 422 | validation error | False |
| New name is reserved | 422 | validation error | False |
| Cannot rename user directory | 500 | internal error | False |

### Error Paths

- **New name same as current** → returns nil (no-op) → 204
- **Name already exists** → ctx.APIError → 422
- **Name reserved/invalid** → ctx.APIError → 422
- **Filesystem rename fails** → ctx.APIErrorInternal → 500

## ⚠️ Performance Issues

| Severity | Type | Description | Recommendation |
|----------|------|-------------|----------------|
| medium | synchronous_blocking | Filesystem directory rename is performed inside the transaction commit path. If the filesystem is slow (NFS), this blocks the request. | Consider performing filesystem rename after transaction commit with rollback logic |

## 🛡️ Resiliency

**Risk Level:** medium

| Pattern | Status | Severity | Detail |
|---------|--------|----------|--------|
| non_atomic | ❌ missing | medium | Filesystem rename happens before transaction commit. If commit fails, code attempts rollback of filesystem rename, but if rollback also fails, state is inconsistent (filesystem renamed but DB not updated). |
| idempotency | ✅ configured | low | If new_name == current name, returns 204 immediately (no-op). Uniqueness check prevents conflicts. |

**Non-atomic operations:**
- ⚠️ Filesystem rename + DB transaction commit are not atomic; partial failure can leave inconsistent state

**Cascading failure risk:** Filesystem failure after DB changes could leave org in broken state

**Graceful degradation:** Rollback attempted on commit failure
